source.title: EmoRSS: Mitigating Emotion-Induced Over-Refusal in Large Language Models
source.authors: Shu-Yi Miao; Yao-Jin Ma; Chen-Hang Cui; Xiao-Hao Liu; Ji-Sheng Dang; Sheng-Da Zhuo; Fei Shen; Tat-Seng Chua

record.tranche_reason: The study causally steers a probe-derived refusal direction and an SAE refusal subspace, and measures refusal behavior. Its method differs from the original difference-in-means direction and it does not ablate that direction at every layer and position.
record.gate_note: The study's own direction and subspace interventions, matched emotional-request reversals, single-direction comparison, and intervention-layer comparison report outcomes bearing on the claim. Probe ROC-AUC is used to select a layer and direction, so those selection values are not recorded as result rows. Results cited from other studies are excluded.
record.test_reason: Section 3.4 (Tables 1–2, Fig. 4) steers a logistic-probe refusal direction and its SAE-projected variant at one layer. It measures benign refusal and the first-token refusal margin against random controls, a different method aimed at V1's causal question. Table 5 also runs the original directional-ablation method (MDA, Arditi et al.) as a baseline on emotional requests. Most other rows concern reversing an emotion-induced shift, which is a different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also claim, from Tables 1–2, that the probe direction and subspace 'causally control model refusal behaviour'. Their 'single global direction is insufficient' statement concerns capturing the emotion-induced shift, not refusal in general. They also acknowledge that Qwen HCR rises from 0.52% to 2.08% under EmoRSS.
record.recipe_differences: Uses layer-wise logistic probes on regular requests to derive a refusal direction, selects aligned SAE decoder features to form a subspace, and intervenes at a selected layer. It does not derive the direction from harmful-minus-harmless mean activations or ablate it across all layers and positions.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome depends on intervention direction and layer. At ρ = 1, Qwen3-8B opposite-direction steering lowers first-token refusal margin but raises complete-response BRR. The selected refusal-sensitive layer gives lower BRR than adjacent or final layers in the reported comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: Emotional preambles shift benign requests toward refusal along the probe refusal direction, in first-token margin and in refusal rate (Fig. 5); harmful requests show no consistent shift.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Emotional framing of benign requests moves activations along the refusal direction and increases over-refusal.

fits_no_version.finding: Reversing the emotion-induced shift with an SAE-feature-confined vector reduces emotional over-refusal more than matched reversal along w or a random direction. At ρ=20 the gap is clearer on Llama (BRR 7.29 vs 17.19).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Correcting emotion-induced over-refusal works better with a vector confined to refusal-aligned SAE features than with the global refusal direction.

fits_no_version.finding: EmoRSS works best at the probe-selected layer, compared with the adjacent and final layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Over-refusal steering effectiveness depends on intervening at the refusal-sensitive layer.

record.problems: Only two models are tested. The direct causal interventions are at a selected layer rather than all layers and positions. Tables 1–4 do not report uncertainty estimates; the paper reports 95% confidence intervals for other analyses. The authors state that the stronger evaluation strengths are amplified steering and should not be interpreted as exact cancellation or as the fraction of refusal behavior causally mediated by the selected features.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted to meet the row cap. Did not record probe ROC-AUC values used to select the layer, cited results from other work, or general-capability results for methods other than the tested direction/subspace intervention.

untested.parts: No harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction from the study itself, and no all-layer, all-position ablation of its own direction. At ρ=1, steering is scored on benign-request refusal (BRR) only, not on refusal of harmful requests. No capability check is reported for the Tables 1–2 interventions.
No weight edit or abliterated model.
No jailbreak mechanism or adversarial training.
The 'refusal subspace' interventions use a single projected direction (u_ref) or a single decoded vector (v_emo). There is no multi-dimensional, affine or cone account of refusal.
Qwen3-8B is used, but reasoning versus non-reasoning behaviour is not examined.

missing.what: MDA (Arditi et al. directional ablation) baseline results on emotional requests. Llama: HCR avg 3.65, BRR avg 26.05 vs default 0.00/21.35. Qwen: HCR 2.08, BRR 11.46 vs default 0.52/22.91. Implementation details are not given.
Dose-response of u_ref steering. BRR rises with +ρ and falls with −ρ, and HCR rises under stronger reverse steering, with 95% CIs. Exact values are hard to read from the figure text.
General capability (MMLU, XSum) for the 'Refusal Direction' intervention; text says it stays close to the unmodified model.

record.verdict_notes: The 'refusal subspace' steering in Tables 1–2 uses u_ref, one normalized direction, so it does not bear on V4. The paper's statement that refusal-direction effects exceed random controls is false for Qwen BRR: refusal and random give identical values, 8.85 and 8.33. The reader's V4 labels are dropped. The MDA baseline is the closest test of the original method, but the study does not say how the direction was derived or which layers were ablated.

versions.untested_parts: Does not use the original harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction; does not ablate one direction at every layer and position; does not establish that ablation removes most or all refusals. General capability is not measured for the direct single-direction interventions in Tables 1–2.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
Does not test whether jailbreaks suppress the refusal direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
Tests a probe-derived direction against a selected SAE refusal subspace, but does not test an affine or cone model.
Does not separate harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
No cross-language, base-to-instruct, or model-variant transfer test.
Does not vary refusal training or its timing.
